nodes.text: Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that in any $2$-colouring of the subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ there is always a monochromatic family of at least $f(n)$ sets which is closed under taking unions and intersections. Estimate $f(n)$. Let $F(n)$ be defined similarly, except that we only require the family be closed under taking unions. Estimate $F(n)$. In particular, is it true that $F(n)\geq n^{\omega(n)}$ for some $\omega(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$, and $F(n)<(1+o(1))^n$?

#1183 : [Er78,p.39] combinatorics | ramsey theory A problem of Erdős and Ulam. It is trivial that $f(n)\geq \frac{n+1}{2}$, since there is a sequence of $n+1$ many nested subsets. This seems to be all that they knew; Erdős [Er78] wrote 'we have no plausible conjecture for the true order of magnitude of $f(n)$'. They similarly had no good guess about $F(n)$. In [Er78] Erdős wrote that if the colouring is such that all subsets of same size receive the same colour then Howorka had proved that $F(n)>n^{\omega(n)}$ for some $\omega(n)\to \infty$, but gave no reference.
